newsitem.title: ITALY: Eni, Fiat in environmental venture.
newsitem.headline: Eni, Fiat in environmental venture.

text.p: Car maker Fiat and energy group Eni will join forces in a research programme aimed at developing environmentally-friendly engines and fuels, the two Italian giants said in a joint statement.

The research will concentrate on the use of natural gas for car engines, but will also test new diesel and petrol mixes which "strongly reduce polluting substances and components," the statement said.

"The deal foresees an initial two years of research and experimentation into the most advanced motoring technologies, reformulating combustible fuels and a commitment to develop alternative engines and fuels," Eni and Fiat said.
In particular, the firms said they aimed to reduce the sulphur content in petrol to 100 parts per one million from 200 parts.
The first concrete results in this field should be seen in engines for public transport vehicles.
For cars, Eni and Fiat said they expected to work on new methane technology would provide the biggest step forward.

Fiat has said it will soon launch a new version of its recently unveiled medium-to-large car, the Marea, which runs off a methane/petrol mix. It is also working on a prototype with a methane-only engine.
Eni said in Friday's statement that it was committed to expanding the number of its Agip petrol distribution outlets which would supply the natural gas fuel.
The statement gave no financial details of the project.
